diagnostic_evidence.quote: E-AO and SRPL are instead designed to be fast heuristics, but they only converge to stationary points.
Observe also that any solution pair and all local minima of $\SV(A,P,Q)$ are Nash pairs.

issues.failure_explanation: Stationarity or blockwise optimality does not imply local minimality. For example, with unrestricted cones and $A=\operatorname{diag}(2,1)$, the AO updates leave $(u,v)=(-e_2,e_2)$ fixed, although its value $-1$ is not a local minimum: simultaneous rotations toward the first singular directions decrease the value. The paper itself later only claims convergence to stationary points.

failure_location.quote: The other two are heuristics, meaning that they rapidly compute locally optimal solutions;

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the local-optimality promise by the weaker statement that the methods seek stationary or blockwise stationary points, consistently with the later numerical section.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract and contribution summary overstate the guarantee supplied by E-AO and SRPL; their outputs cannot generally be described as locally optimal.
issues.title: Heuristics are incorrectly advertised as computing local optima
issues.why_classification: The supported repair changes the advertised guarantee type from local optimality to stationarity, a substantive weakening rather than a routine clarification.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
The subproblem in $u$ is expressed as
\[u  = \argmin_{x \in P} \langle x,Av\rangle
 \; \text{ such that } \; \|x\|=1,\]

issues.failure_explanation: The set $P\cap\{x:\|x\|=1\}$ is generally nonconvex; for instance, in $P=\mathbb R_+^2$, both canonical vectors are feasible while their midpoint is not. Thus the displayed and algorithmic subproblems are not convex as claimed. The preceding convex relaxation uses $\|x\|\leq1$, but the actual AO and E-AO updates revert to equality constraints, and no argument is supplied that the cited convergence result applies to these updates or to the extrapolated/restarted scheme.

failure_location.quote: In our case, the subproblems are convex and the feasible sets are compact, hence AO is guaranteed to have a subsequence converging to a critical pair~\cite{grippo2000convergence}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either withdraw the convergence guarantee or provide a convergence argument applicable to the unit-sphere block problems and the extrapolation/restart mechanism; merely invoking convex block optimization is insufficient.
issues.overall_effect: The stated subsequential convergence guarantee for the proposed AO methodology is unsupported as written, although the algorithms may still be used heuristically.
issues.title: AO convergence justification treats nonconvex sphere sections as convex
issues.why_classification: The algorithms remain usable as explicitly advertised heuristics, but retaining the convergence claim requires a contained nontrivial argument or a carefully modified algorithm.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, by denoting $\Delta_d:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d: x\geq 0,\, \langle e,x\rangle = 1\}$, the probability simplex in $\mathbb R^d$, \eqref{frac1} becomes

issues.failure_explanation: Because $d_1^k=\tilde x^k-x^k$ and both endpoints lie in the simplex, the update is guaranteed to remain in the simplex only for $0\leq t_k\leq1$. The stated assumptions permit $\beta>1$, and the line search may accept $\ell_k=0$, giving $t_k=\beta>1$. Such extrapolation beyond $\tilde x^k$ can create negative coordinates, so subsequent evaluations need not be feasible for problem \eqref{frac2}.

failure_location.quote: \REQUIRE Matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, polyhedral cones $P=G(\mathbb R^p_+)$ and $Q=H(\mathbb R^q_+)$; initial points $x^0\in\Delta_p$, $y^0\in\Delta_q$; prox-parameters  $\mu_1,\mu_2\geq0$; line-search algorithm parameters $\beta>0$, $0<\alpha<1$, $0<\rho<1$;

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require $0<\beta\leq1$ or otherwise cap every accepted step at one, ensuring that each update is a convex combination of two simplex points.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm SRPL is not well defined on its full stated parameter range and can violate its simplex invariant.
issues.title: SRPL line search can leave the probability simplices
issues.why_classification: A short local restriction on the line-search parameter restores feasibility without changing the method, objective, rate claims, or advertised scope.
